Hi Olga,

Hope you're well. As part of our SOC 2 scoping for Nimbus' integration with Redwood Dedicated/Private deployments, our auditors have asked for a concise set of artifacts that demonstrate network demarcation and isolation between customer workloads and Redwood control plane/management functions. Specifically they are asking for: 

- A logical network diagram that shows the "airlock"/demarcation layers for Dedicated and Private deployments (control plane, data plane, management, egress)
- A short narrative (1–2 pages) explaining how you enforce tenant isolation at the networking layer, including how KMS boundaries and egress paths are controlled
- Evidence of routing and firewall policy enforcement (ACL examples, NACLs, NGFW rules) or a reference to a canonical ruleset

Would you be able to provide those artifacts (PDF/diagram + short narrative) by EOD Friday 2027-11-12? If there's a single consolidated file you prefer we accept, that works too.

Auditors have also requested a contact on your side who can run a 30-minute walkthrough of the diagram and any assumptions (technical reviewer).

Thanks — Diana

Hi Diana — thanks for the clear ask. We can absolutely provide a consolidated evidence packet and a walkthrough. I've attached the current set of artifacts we use for SOC/attestation requests and provided a short summary below.

Attachments: private-dedicated-airlock-diagram-v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB); controlplane-segmentation-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 180 KB)

Quick summary (high level):
- Logical demarcation: we separate traffic into four planes — Control Plane, Management Plane (ops), Customer Data Plane (tenant VMs/containers), and Egress/Out-of-band. The attached diagram labels edge demarcation points, VPC peering vs. transit, and the dedicated GPU pools.
- Enforcement primitives: segmentation is enforced via a combination of cloud-native VPC constructs (subnet ACLs), per-tenant routing tables, and firewall rules at the edge (NGFW). For Dedicated deployments, we place tenant compute in isolated subnets behind a tenant-specific NAT gateway and edge ACLs.
- KMS boundary: customer keys never traverse the control plane. We maintain a strict KMS access control list and per-tenant envelope keys when customers opt for customer-managed keys. Key access is audited via a dedicated KMS audit trail that is part of the controlplane-segmentation-matrix.xlsx.
- Egress controls: egress is forced through an audited proxy cluster; outbound flows are tagged and logged. For regulated customers we can provide an egress allowlist and attest to no-default Internet routes for tenant subnets.

Planned next steps:
1) I've attached the diagram and segmentation matrix for your auditors to review.
2) Karthik (copied) will add a short technical note clarifying NAT, KV cache boundary, and control-plane-to-data-plane channels.
3) We can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on Thursday or Friday — I included a Calendly link below.

If you need a one-page auditor summary, we will include a separate PDF (I can draft and attach by EOD Thursday).

Best,

Hi Diana / Olga — adding a few technical clarifications auditors often ask for: 

- NAT and route ownership: tenant subnets in Dedicated deployments use tenant-specific routing tables; SNAT is applied at the tenant NAT gateway so return-path separation is deterministic. We do not perform hairpin NAT from control-plane hosts into tenant subnets.
- Control plane access: the control plane communicates to the data plane over dedicated, authenticated control channels on a private management network. These channels are one-way for orchestration commands; ephemeral certificates are rotated every 24 hours.
- KV cache isolation: every model-serving instance has an isolated KV cache namespace. We enforce namespace scoping at the runtime layer and block cross-tenant KV namespace access through runtime policy.
- Firewall examples: the attached controlplane-segmentation-matrix.xlsx includes representative SG/ACL snippets and a mapping to CAIQ/OSS-CA references.
- Proof artifacts: aside from diagrams, auditors typically accept a sample flow capture (redacted IPs) showing control plane handshake and a signed statement from infra owning team. If useful we can produce a redacted pcap and a one-page attestation.

I'll prepare the one-page summary Olga mentioned and attach the CAIQ mapping workbook (doing that now).

Thanks — Karthik
